haiku-low.q1: A pull request runs build and make test-unit only, with no push and no deploy. A merge to main (push to main) starts the run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: registry.internal/shop-api:<SHA>, the full merged commit SHA. It is built once in step 1 on the merge, and every later step deploys that tag without rebuilding.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure: one automatic retry; if it fails, the run ends, unit job is cancelled, and it announces. Unit failure: no retry, run ends, integration job cancelled, announces.
haiku-low.q4: Smoke failure triggers deploy.sh rollback staging, restoring the image on previous_tag with schema still migrated. Previous_tag is read from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag; run then ends and announces.
haiku-low.q5: Any member of release-approvers except the merged commit's author. If no approval within 72 hours, the expiry end runs: nothing goes to production, locks released, announced in #deploys.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. The deploy.sh script writes both only after a rollout succeeds; the pipeline only reads current_tag.
haiku-low.q7: Canary-off scales the canary to 0 pods. Stable is not rolled back, recorded tags are unchanged (canary never recorded in SSM), and the migrated schema stays, since nothing undoes migrations.
haiku-low.q8: It is superseded: a neutral end, not a failure. It deploys nothing, releases its locks, and posts a short note in #deploys.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits for the next window opening, with the 72-hour deadline still applying. While another production deploy holds the lock it queues, then rechecks the window and superseded status after taking the lock.
haiku-low.q10: The 1-minute canary 5xx ratio from Prometheus, sampled every 30 s for 15 min from the first ready pod. Fails on any sample above 1 percent, or 2 minutes of no data.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED how approvers are notified. The approval is a CI manual job limited to release-approvers, with a 72-hour deadline, and it records who approved and when.
haiku-low.q12: Not automatically. Staging deploy failure: no rollback, a human decides. Production: canary-off, then a human chooses roll-forward or rollback, because previous_tag is two releases back if tags were not written.

sonnet.q1: A pull request event runs a CI image build plus make test-unit (no push, no deploy); result is a check on the PR. A push to main (merge) starts the run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the single image registry.internal/shop-api:<full commit SHA>, built and pushed once in step 1. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: one automatic retry; if the retry fails, the run ends (failure), the unit job is cancelled, and it is announced in #deploys. Unit test failure: no retry; the run ends, the integration job is cancelled, and it is announced.
sonnet.q4: The pipeline runs deploy.sh rollback staging, then the run ends as a failure with an announcement. Staging returns to previous_tag, read from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag, which the script wrote after the successful deploy. Only the image is restored; the schema stays migrated.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, and not the author of the merged commit (that approval is discarded and the gate stays open). If no one approves within 72 h of the request, the run ends in expiry: nothing goes to production, locks are released, and it is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes both only after a successful rollout of the stable deployment. The pipeline never writes them. The canary is not recorded there.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment is untouched and still running its old image. SSM tags are unchanged (the canary is never recorded and the tags are written only by a production deploy). canary-off scales the canary to 0 pods. The database schema stays migrated forward, because deploy.sh canary ran migrate and nothing undoes migrations. The run fails, the lock is released and it is announced.
sonnet.q8: The older run is superseded: it ends in a neutral (amber) superseded end with no deploy, locks released, and a short note posted in #deploys. The check runs after approval (staging current_tag is now a newer commit) and again after taking the production lock.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits for the next window opening (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC), subject to the 72 h deadline from the approval request, which ends in expiry if passed. If another production deploy holds the production-deploy lock: it queues behind the lock, and when it gets the lock it re-checks the window (if closed, releases the lock and waits again) and then runs the superseded check against production current_tag. The 72 h deadline also applies to the lock wait.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio in Prometheus: sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="shop-api-canary",code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{app="shop-api-canary"}[1m])). A CI watch step samples it every 30 s for 15 minutes, starting when deploy.sh canary returns. Failure: any single sample above 1 percent, or 2 minutes of no data.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document says nobody is notified automatically about the approval gate being open, in the context of discarded author approvals. It does not describe any notification to approvers, or what information they see beyond the CI approval job recording who approved and when.
sonnet.q12: Staging: if deploy.sh staging itself fails, there is no rollback because tags were not written, so previous_tag would be two releases back and a rollback would overshoot. The run just ends and announces. Production: if deploy.sh production fails, there is no automatic rollback either, for the same reason. canary-off runs, the run fails and announces, and a human chooses between rolling forward and deploy.sh rollback production. The document does not say how the environment is returned to a known image automatically; it may be left part rolled out.
